from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        point_b = Dot(color="#E74C3C")

        self.place_at_grid(point_b, 'E5')

        label_b.next_to(point_b, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Write(Text("The Brachistochrone Problem", color=WHITE, font_size=32).move_to(self.grid['A3'])))
        self.play(FadeIn(point_a), FadeIn(point_b), FadeIn(label_a), FadeIn(label_b))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        straight_path = Line(point_a.get_center(), point_b.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(straight_path))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        # Creating a curve using a CubicBezier
        curve = CubicBezier(point_a.get_center(), self.grid['C4'], self.grid['D4'], point_b.get_center(), color="#3498DB")
        self.play(Create(curve))
        
        ball = Dot(color="#F1C40F")
        ball.move_to(point_a.get_center())
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(ball, curve), run_time=2)
        
        dashed_line = DashedLine(point_a.get_center(), point_b.get_center(), color="#2ECC71")
        self.play(Create(dashed_line))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Brachistochrone curve is a cycloid.",
            "Traced by a point on a rolling circle.",
            "It balances distance and speed perfectly.",
            "Accelerate rapidly, then cruise to B.",
            "This is the fastest possible path."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Solution: The Cycloid", lecture_lines)
        
        r = 0.5
        
        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 1 ---
        # Display a cycloid curve generated by a rolling circle. (Color: #1ABC9C)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#1ABC9C"))
        
        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 2 ---
        # Animate the circle rolling along a horizontal line. (Color: #FFFFFF)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 3 ---
        # Trace the path of a point on the circle's edge. (Color: #3498DB)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        
        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 4 ---
        # Highlight the cycloid path as the fastest route. (Color: #E74C3C)
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))
        
        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 5 ---
        # Show the cycloid equation: x = r(θ - sinθ), y = r(1 - cosθ). (Color: #F1C40F)
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        
        # Visuals
        # Circle
        circle = Circle(radius=r, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C2')
        
        # Cycloid Path
        def cycloid_func(t):
            return np.array([r * (t - np.sin(t)), -r * (1 - np.cos(t)), 0])
        
        cycloid = ParametricFunction(cycloid_func, t_range=[0, 2*PI], color="#1ABC9C")
        self.place_at_grid(cycloid, 'C2')
        
        # Point on rim
        dot = Dot(color="#3498DB")
        self.add(dot)
        
        # Rolling animation
        # Note: The cycloid is generated by rolling a circle on a line.
        line = Line(start=self.grid['B1'], end=self.grid['B6'], color=WHITE)
        self.add(line)
        
        # Use value tracker to animate
        theta = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def update_circle(c):
            t = theta.get_value()
            c.move_to(np.array([1.5 + r * t, 0.5, 0]))
            
        def update_dot(d):
            t = theta.get_value()
            d.move_to(np.array([1.5 + r * t + r * np.sin(t), 0.5 - r * np.cos(t), 0]))
            
        circle.add_updater(update_circle)
        dot.add_updater(update_dot)
        
        self.add(circle, dot, cycloid)
        self.play(theta.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Equation
        eq = MathTex("x = r(\\theta - \\sin\\theta), \\quad y = r(1 - \\cos\\theta)", color="#F1C40F")
        self.place_at_grid(eq, 'F3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(eq))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conceptual Insight: Why it Works", [
            "Cycloid optimizes the trade-off.",
            "Vertical drops steal gravitational speed.",
            "Levels off to maintain momentum.",
            "It acts like a cheetah's sprint.",
            "Path shape creates optimal transit."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        # 1. Display two different potential paths
        path1 = Line(start=[-1, 1, 0], end=[1, -1, 0], color=WHITE)
        path2 = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([2 * (t - np.sin(t)), -2 * (1 - np.cos(t)), 0]),
            t_range=[0, PI], color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_at_grid(path1, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(path2, 'E4')
        self.play(Create(path1), Create(path2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # 2. Animate the ball on the cycloid moving faster
        ball = Dot(color="#2ECC71")
        self.place_at_grid(ball, 'E2')
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(ball, path2, run_time=2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#E67E22"))

        # 3. Use color shift to show acceleration change
        path2_shifted = path2.copy().set_color("#E67E22")
        self.play(Transform(path2, path2_shifted))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))
        
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Calculus of Variations found the solution.", "Time is independent of start point.", "Applied in efficient modern engineering."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Real-world Application", lecture_lines)

outline.topic: The Brachistochrone Problem: The Race of Curves

sections.title: The Hook: Defining the Challenge
sections.content: Introduce the problem: A bead slides down a wire from point A to point B under gravity. Which path takes the shortest time? Contrast the intuitive 'straight line' against the 'curved path' using a split-screen animation.
sections.example: Compare a roller coaster designer choosing a straight slope versus a curved 'drop' to reach the bottom fastest.

sections.title: Prerequisites: Energy vs. Time
sections.content: Briefly review Conservation of Energy (v = sqrt(2gh)). Explain why the path is not just about distance (the straight line), but about speed (gaining height early to maximize velocity).
sections.example: Visual graph showing how a steeper initial drop increases velocity earlier, even if the total path distance is longer.

sections.title: The Solution: The Cycloid
sections.content: Reveal the Brachistochrone curve: The Cycloid. Visualize it as the path traced by a point on the rim of a rolling circle. Use an animation overlaying a cycloid path on a grid to show the 'accelerate, then cruise' strategy.
sections.example: An animation of a wheel rolling along a ceiling, with a highlighted red dot marking the cycloid trajectory from A to B.

sections.title: Conceptual Insight: Why it Works
sections.content: Explain the balance: The cycloid optimizes the trade-off between path length and gravitational acceleration. It 'steals' speed by dropping vertically, then levels off to utilize that speed.
sections.example: Compare a cheetah (which accelerates rapidly) to a marathon runner; the cycloid is the 'cheetah' of geometric paths.

sections.title: Summary & Real-world Application
sections.content: Conclude with the Brachistochrone's legacy in the Calculus of Variations. Mention the Tautochrone property (the curve where time is independent of starting position).
sections.example: Visualizing how this principle is used in high-speed rail track design and water-slide engineering for optimal transit times.
